uncertainties.finding: The /obs-snapshot path does not exist anywhere in the pinned tree (absence check: 0 matches). Catalog apps are served as static bundles from apps/<slug> through workspaceService.serveApp, and every owner JSON API passes the shared owner-route boundary (host and origin gate, credential header only, constant-time match). Existing same-shaped precedents are /api/acdd-evidence and the /api/run-traces owner route.
uncertainties.extension_seam: R16/R17 attach /api/rizzstack/rails/* as a new owner-route module registered by exact path in server/index.mjs (following the technologyOwnerRoute pattern); GET routes stay read-only behind the owner boundary, mutations only through the trusted owner principal, and the catalog pane stays read-only unless owner mutation capability is proven (spec section 7 default: trusted shell dialog).
uncertainties.residual: The deployed host's own router or reverse-proxy configuration is deployment-side and not in any repo; it must be rechecked at R17 admission before production registration.

uncertainties.question: Does the bundlebees action queue expose a stable committed operation identity with fencing, idempotency and replayable transition history?
uncertainties.reason: The fenced action-queue interface the spec requires does not exist in the pinned bundlebees tree. queue.py is a feature-queue pointer over the job store (intake, durable claim, one-pass consumption) with no operation identity, no fencing epoch and no authority revalidation; work_scheduler.py is a coordinator claim queue serialized by a lock file with atomic replaces, again with no fencing semantics; the launcher adapter explicitly records that no server-enforced idempotency exists yet; and a case-insensitive search for fencing across the plugin package returns zero matches. The queue the spec calls user-reported in flight is not in this tree, so its eventual operation identity, idempotency and reconciliation semantics cannot be cited from evidence and are not guessed here.

uncertainties.finding: The deployed stream is attempt-level: state records, heartbeat records, and worker-prefixed passthrough records whose upstream kinds are turn_started, message, turn_ended, error and exited. It contains no tool-level start or finish records, so tool.start/tool.finish rails events cannot be paired from the native log; tool-call granularity exists only in the Hermes message stream (vibeline sessions pairing by tool_call_id). No rotation was observed: one append-only file per attempt, with restart replay of terminal receipts and durable outbox export positions providing the final receipt identity. The sanitized trace fixture in this matrix mirrors exactly this shape.
uncertainties.downstream_rule: R08's launcher-log adapter must emit attempt-level lane events with worker-prefixed kinds normalized through fixture-versioned parsers, dedupe native and backfilled records on (attempt_id, lseq), and never fabricate tool pairs or durations; tool-level timing comes from the Hermes-session source where present.
uncertainties.residual: Upstream worker kinds arrive from the worker runtime and may evolve; the fixture-versioned parser must be rechecked at R08 admission per the spec section 2 recheck rule.
